1.mascotDialogue: A collision here is not an error — it is an outcome the entire design anticipates. Each bucket simply becomes a small linked list instead of a single slot.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 13 is the entire strategy — rather than overwrite whatever is already in the bucket, the new node points at it and becomes the new head. Nothing is ever lost to a collision.

3.mascotDialogue: Bucket 3 now carries a two-node chain — 17, inserted after 10, lands at the head, exactly as insert-at-head predicts.

4.mascotDialogue: The chain appears perfectly fine — one node, no dangling pointer in sight. This is the trap. The bug is not a broken pointer, it is a silently vanished one, and the app renders 'lost node' explicitly so it does not remain invisible.
